interpretation: At n=11 (3 correct + 8 hallucinated), this test only reaches 80% power to distinguish from chance (AUROC=0.5) in the helpful direction once the true held-out AUROC is approximately 0.95, or in the anti-predictive direction once it is approximately 0.05. The observed point estimates in the kernel output (0.0-0.125) sit inside the well-powered anti-predictive region at this n, which is exactly why the exact Mann-Whitney tests on the same data are nominally significant (anti-predictive) at 3 of 4 cells -- this test is well-powered to detect a true AUROC this far below chance, so that nominal significance is not itself surprising or informative about a real anti-predictive relationship; it does not, however, resolve whether the true held-out AUROC is actually anti-predictive or simply appears so due to chance fluctuation at n=11, since a single realization cannot distinguish the two without more data. The test remains uninformative about whether the direction carries any *helpful* signal (AUROC > 0.5), which would require a true AUROC of 0.95 to detect at 80% power -- far above anything plausible here.
